UX REVIEW · SEPTEMBER 12, 2026

Vigilon Cyber and XtraByte

Evidence appendix for the homepage overhaul guidance. These are captures of the live sites, not redesign mockups.

Recommendation: Keep Vigilon’s specialist positioning and reading-friendly surfaces. Bring over XtraByte’s atmospheric video and restrained card feedback. Make the first substantive homepage section a guided choice of customer tasks, and provide immediate, explained results before contact capture.

Sources: Vigilon homepage · XtraByte homepage · Vigilon inquiry path

Limits: Visual and DOM-based review, including mobile layouts and observed interaction styling. No conversion analytics, customer usability sessions, real-device testing, full keyboard/screen-reader audit, performance benchmark, form submission or Continuum feature verification. Default desktop viewport sizes differed between tabs; phone views used a 390px width. Findings describe observed states rather than proving audience retention.

  2. XtraByte desktop hero — Strong visual presence; refine
  3. XtraByte service cards — Useful interaction pattern; dense

1. Vigilon desktop hero

Strong foundation; simplify

Clear brand, left-aligned copy and prominent orange action. The long introductory paragraph and large empty right side reduce first-screen efficiency. Replace the statistics strip with useful task choices.

2. XtraByte desktop hero

Strong visual presence; refine

Muted looping MP4 provides atmospheric movement. Centered, shorter copy is easy to scan, but infrastructure positioning is too broad for the new product-compliance offer. No visible pause control was found.

3. XtraByte service cards

Useful interaction pattern; dense

Images and a visible highlighted card create depth. Inspected styles specify a 5px lift, border/shadow change and 1.05 image scale. Carry over restrained feedback; reduce homepage detail and replace generic security pictures with specific evidence.

4. Vigilon service cards

Readable; reorganize

Light surfaces support reading. Six peer cards mix regulations with testing methods. Prioritize RED testing, CRA technical documentation and Continuum, with a separate route to other standards and assessments.

5. Vigilon trust section

Relevant claims; add evidence

Regulatory knowledge, assessment-path support and actionable reporting fit the buyer. Add a sample deliverable and an attributed case study. Clarify the scope of remediation and retesting commitments.

6. XtraByte trust section

Useful topics; verify claims

Named partnership, methods and continued support are worth considering. Screenshot captures the beginning of this section; full text was read in the accessibility tree. Verify current credentials and accreditation status before reuse. Decorative cards should not signal clickability if they do not act.

7. Vigilon mobile hero

Needs shorter copy

At a 390px viewport the paragraph consumes many lines and puts the primary action near the lower edge of the first screen. Shorten the headline and description; keep the primary action early.

8. XtraByte mobile hero

Engaging; overflow issue

The primary action appears earlier than on Vigilon. A horizontal scrollbar is visible; DOM inspection found a roughly 750px document at a 390px viewport, with the off-screen navigation extending beyond the viewport. Fix this before transferring layout code.

9. Vigilon mobile navigation

Works visually; accessibility issue

Opening the menu exposed navigation visually, but the toggle remained announced as collapsed in the accessibility tree. Verify and synchronize expanded state. Make service groups explicit tap-controlled disclosures.

10. Vigilon quote introduction

Helpful expectations; ambiguous timing

The next-step explanation is reassuring, but a quote within 24 hours is ambiguous when consultation and scoping come first. Specify the event that starts the promised response period. The form begins below the first viewport.

11. Vigilon inquiry form

Suitable for scoped leads; heavy for discovery

Multiple contact fields precede product context. Keep a direct quote route for ready buyers, but use short product questions and immediate results for uncertain visitors. Reuse their answers in any subsequent inquiry. No form was submitted.
